clue.text: Large glasses leading to heart slogan displayed by motorist (13, two words)

parts.note: bumpers are glasses filled to the brim
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A cardiologist's warning about big drinks, turned into a car slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper sticker is a printed slogan stuck on a car's rear fender for other drivers to read.

clue.text: Supports crib to give mutual favours

parts.note: to back is to support
a cratch is a crib or manger for fodder

explanation.surface: A cheat's crib sheet propping up a deal of mutual favours.
explanation.definitionFit: To backscratch is to trade favours, from the idiom you scratch my back and I'll scratch yours.

clue.text: Mouse enclosed within old wall

indicators.note: enclosed means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: mure is an archaic word for a wall
in means within

explanation.surface: A mouse trapped inside an ancient wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Murine means of mice or a mouse-like rodent, so as a noun or adjective it stands for a mouse.

clue.text: Adult type of sclerosis in hand? This makes tricky incision

indicators.note: in sets the abbreviations inside the word for a hand

parts.note: a paw is an animal's hand, jokingly a hand
A is the film certificate for adult
disseminated sclerosis, the old name for multiple sclerosis

explanation.surface: A medical note about a nerve disease in the hand making surgery tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface suggests a scalpel; the definition is a tool, the wordplay sits after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A padsaw is a small narrow saw for cutting curves or keyholes, so it makes awkward cuts.

clue.text: Attachment for outback safari? Rumpus when last is lost, we hear! (6, two words)

indicators.note: losing the last means dropping the final letter of the word
we hear means the result is judged by its sound

parts.note: rhubarb is the noise of a crowd, here missing its final letter

explanation.surface: An Australian tour vehicle with a noisy argument on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb is the word actors mutter for crowd noise, so it means a hubbub.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo bar is a metal grille on the front of a vehicle to protect it from kangaroos in the Australian outback.

clue.text: Epic tales? Second's a delight

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
taken as written
a gas is a great pleasure or lark

explanation.surface: A reader praising the second instalment of an epic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Second's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long heroic narratives, such as the Norse family stories, so they are epics.

clue.text: Having had a brainwave I exploit, retaining one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retaining means holding on, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: an exploit is a deed
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of exploiting an idea of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideaed, also spelt idea'd, means furnished with ideas, so having conceived a sudden inspiration.

clue.text: Name associated with giant mincer never includes it

indicators.note: the phrase that includes it holds the letters within its words

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A giant who never puts anything through a mincer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cerne Abbas Giant is a huge chalk figure cut into a Dorset hillside in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerne is the name of the village and river linked with the famous chalk hill figure.

clue.text: Brain disease universal among West African people

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the Kru are a people of Liberia
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A neurological illness spreading widely in a West African population.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuru is a fatal prion disease of the brain once found among the Fore people of New Guinea.

clue.text: Conifer portions are chopped up

indicators.note: chopping up breaks something into bits that land in a jumble

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pieces of a felled pine tree cut into firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinospora is a horticultural name for juvenile forms of cypress, evergreen cone-bearing trees.

clue.text: Surfing accessory: sailor's alongside, as having entered

indicators.note: something that has entered sits inside another word, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: in nautical usage aboard can mean alongside a ship
qua is Latin for in the capacity of, i.e. as

explanation.surface: A beach checklist noting a sailor stands next to some board.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word goes in after the first A of the sailor's term.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquaboard is a type of board ridden on waves, a piece of surfing equipment.

clue.text: Experiencing ecstasy with grass around? Took ill

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the grass word goes outside

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
sent means carried away with rapture

explanation.surface: A drug-taker on ecstasy and cannabis who then felt sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took ill' looks like falling sick, but it is the idiom to take something ill, i.e. be offended by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a thing ill is to be offended by it, which is what resenting it means.

clue.text: I'll be pursuing one in pack, woolly

indicators.note: what is pursuing comes behind, so the letter follows the other piece

parts.note: one item in a pack of cards
I taken as written; the 'll (will) just joins it to the verb

explanation.surface: A hunter or player chasing someone in the pack, with a sheep-like twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardi is short for cardigan, and a woolly is a knitted garment, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Prank involving pickled roe that puts you off your food

definitions.text: that puts you off your food

indicators.note: pickled can mean drunk and muddled, so these letters are scrambled
involving means wrapping in, so the prank word surrounds the other

parts.note: an antic is a caper or prank
the word roe, mixed

explanation.surface: A practical joke with pickled fish eggs that kills your appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: An anoretic is an appetite suppressant, a drug that reduces the desire to eat.

clue.text: Rummage around for thin ribbon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to search about busily
second meaning: a narrow tape of cotton or silk

explanation.surface: Someone searching a sewing box for a narrow strip of tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret is to search diligently; a ferret is also a dictionary word for narrow tape used in binding.

clue.text: This Jewish doughball etc, cooking … thickens maybe

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients into a new form, so the letters are mixed up
maybe flags that the longer word is only one possible mix, from which the extra letters are taken out

parts.note: the full word that the cooked combination could make
taken as written, removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: A recipe note: this dumpling and other things, when cooked, thicken the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus ETC, mixed, could give THICKENS; so take ETC from THICKENS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A knish is a baked or fried dough pocket of Jewish Eastern European cookery, often filled with potato.

clue.text: Crustacean genus students found beside Welsh lake

indicators.note: beside puts one piece next to the other, here the students coming after the lake

parts.note: Bala Lake, or Llyn Tegid, is the largest natural lake in Wales
the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Biology students discover a new crustacean while on a field trip by a lake in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Balanus is the scientific genus of acorn barnacles, which are crustaceans.

clue.text: Some tourists on a tack. Pastoral perhaps

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers sailing along a tack through rural countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Pastoral is Beethoven's Sixth Symphony nickname but also his Piano Sonata No. 15; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 15 is known as the Pastoral, so it is one example of the musical form.

clue.text: Give glossy look to veg without (Italian) coating

indicators.note: a coating wraps around what it covers, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: short for senza, Italian for without, a musical direction
a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A chef glazing vegetables without using an Italian-style coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like an outside signal but it is the word being translated; SEN. is the score abbreviation of senza.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleeken is to make smooth and shiny, as with polished hair or fur.

clue.text: Large tree suffering from drought, notice

parts.note: parched from lack of rain
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A big tree wilting in a drought, observed by a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives dryad as a forest tree as well as a wood nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the tree nymph of myth, Chambers records dryad as a name for a large forest tree.

clue.text: One rejecting old coin

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small former French coin

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: deny-er and den-ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier denies or refuses; the denier was also a low-value French coin of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Love being in an apartment and out of debt

indicators.note: being in places the letter inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Happy in your own home and finally solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: To be afloat financially is to stay solvent, keeping one's head above water.

clue.text: Scotch bonnet? In short it's drooping for Jock

indicators.note: in short means shortened, so the word loses a letter as in a poetic elision

parts.note: 't is the clipped form of it, as in 'tis
ourie is Scots for drooping or dreary

explanation.surface: A Scottish chilli pepper, wilting.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch bonnet suggests the chilli, but it is a Scottish cap; 's stands for has. Jock is a nickname for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourie is a Scots word for a bobble on a bonnet and, by extension, the bonnet itself.

clue.text: Cloudy? Sun's come out if not

indicators.note: come out means leave, so a letter departs

parts.note: a cloudy sky is sunless
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: cloudy unless the sun appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun's come out' sounds like clearing weather but means the sun's letter leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless is a conjunction meaning except on condition that, i.e. if not.

clue.text: Look to muscle in repose

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, here the muscle within the word for rest

parts.note: rest is repose
short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: Advice to watch your muscles while relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of respect is to look towards or regard, as one building faces another.

clue.text: Bird from N. America or Peru, very small

parts.note: PE is the international vehicle code for Peru
wee means tiny

explanation.surface: A tiny bird found in North or South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewee is a small American flycatcher, a songbird named for its call.

clue.text: Sloping part of fortification sultan mostly reconstructed

indicators.note: mostly keeps most of the word but not its final letter
reconstructed means rebuilt in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A ruler rebuilding the sloping walls of his fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A talus is the sloping face of a rampart or wall in military architecture.

clue.text: Directly opposes monk having more than half tonsure cut

parts.note: Fr. is short for Friar or Frater, a monk's title

indicators.note: cut as in cutting a pack of cards, which rearranges the order
more than half keeps the greater part of the word, its opening four of seven letters

parts.note: the first four letters of the word

explanation.surface: A monk half-shaved resists something head-on.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection keeps the first four letters, more than half of seven, before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To front something is to face or confront it head-on, so fronts means directly opposes.

clue.text: Church council introducing a Latin series of masses

indicators.note: introducing means the council goes first, bringing in what follows

parts.note: the Council of Trent, the 16th-century Catholic council
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A church council bringing in a Latin series of masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A trental is a set of thirty requiem masses said for the dead, from Latin for thirty.

clue.text: Variety of cider apples? Crop thus spliced maybe

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so these letters are reshuffled
thus spliced points to the mixed letters splitting into the answer plus the word spliced, which is set aside

parts.note: the full fodder
the other word the mixed letters can make, removed

explanation.surface: An orchard question about apple types for cider and grafting a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: CIDER APPLES rearranges into the answer plus SPLICED.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut and gather a harvest, so as a verb it means to crop.

clue.text: To start, my short exchanged for the French tonic?

indicators.note: exchanged for swaps one letter out and puts the other in its place

parts.note: to start is to jump
my cut short to its first letter
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A recipe direction: begin by swapping in a French ingredient for your tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start' looks like an opening instruction, but start is the word to change; the M of the jump word is replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet medicinal drink, and the question mark allows it as an example of a tonic.

clue.text: Ribboned hairpiece that is in fashion

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for that is inside the other word

parts.note: twig is an old word for fashion or style
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A wig tied with a ribbon is now in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-wig was an 18th-century wig with its hair tied at the back with a ribbon.

clue.text: About to revise one's faith

parts.note: c. is the abbreviation of circa, about
to redo is to revise

explanation.surface: Someone poised to rethink their religious beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, a creed, so it is the faith a person holds.

clue.text: Lie square after changing score to draw level

indicators.note: changing alters the arrangement, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Smoothing a lie square on a golf course, then levelling the match score.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an equaliser is the goal that brings a side level with the opposition.

clue.text: Trump's excessive sensitivity? After publicity stunt he's appearing in wild satire

parts.note: hype is promotional fuss

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe at a president thin-skinned about satirical attacks following his own publicity stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's' points to American spelling, without the A of the British hyperaesthesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperesthesia is abnormally heightened sensitivity of the skin or senses, the US spelling of the medical term.
